title: What is your name?
goal: Introduce yourself with 'my name is', ask 'what is your name?', answer 'nice to meet you' with أهلاً, and bounce the question back with 'and you?'.

items.note: She opens with the simplest introduction: أنا (I / I am) + her name, no verb 'to be' needed.

items.mnemonic: ISM: every NAME ends up an '-ISM' (Tom-ism, Julie-ism).

items.en: my name (name + ee = belongs to me)
items.note: The 'ee' sound hooked on the end of a word means it belongs to me: ism (name) → ismee (my name).

items.mnemonic: is-MEE: 'this name IS ME' = MY name.

items.note: أهلاً literally means 'welcome'; it is what you say when you meet someone, so it works as 'nice to meet you'.
items.mnemonic: AH-lan: 'AH, LAND here, welcome!' nice to meet you.

items.note: Swap the -ee (my) for -uka (your, to a man): ismee → ismuka.

items.en: what is your name? (to a male)
items.note: Word for word: what your-name? No 'is'.
أهلاً + the person's name is the natural reply once someone tells you their name.
Quick recap of the three forms before the practice round.

items.ar: ما اسمُكَ؟ اسمي جولي. أهلاً جولي
items.tr: maa ismuka? ismee Julie. ahlan Julie
items.en: What is your name? My name is Julie. Nice to meet you, Julie
items.note: First full mini-exchange: question, answer, welcome.
She contrasts أنا (I) with أنتَ (you) again.
و (and) sticks to the front of أنتَ: wa-anta, said with question intonation.

items.en: my name is Julie, and you?
my name is Tom. Nice to meet you, Tom
the word for 'you' (talking to a man)
items.note: She reminds you أنتَ (anta) is 'you' for a male listener; the female form comes later in the lesson.

items.en: and you, what is your name?

items.ar: اسمي جولي، وأنتَ، ما اسمُكَ؟ اسمي توم. أهلاً توم
items.tr: ismee Julie, wa anta, maa ismuka? ismee Tom. ahlan Tom
items.en: My name is Julie, and you, what is your name? My name is Tom. Nice to meet you, Tom
items.note: The full exchange of the lesson, practised both ways.

items.en: you (to a male), with the -a ending
items.note: She asks which of two endings is right for a man: أنتَ (anta).
Same word as أنتَ but the ending becomes 'i' when you talk to a woman: anta → anti.
She asks for 'name', then 'my name', and checks you do not confuse اسمي with اسمُكَ.
To a woman the ending is -ki instead of -ka: ما اسمُكِ؟ (maa ismuki?).

items.en: what is your name? (to a male / to a female)

dialogue.en: Hello. I am Julie. What is your name?
My name is Ahmad. Nice to meet you, Julie.

dialogue.ar: أنا لستُ من هنا. أنا أتعلّمُ العربية.
dialogue.tr: ana lastu min huna. ana ata'allamu al-'arabiyya.
dialogue.en: I am not from here. I am learning Arabic.

dialogue.tr: anta tafham jayyidan jiddan. wa anti?
dialogue.en: You understand very well. And you (f.)?

dialogue.ar: أنا أفهمُ قليلاً، وأريدُ أن أتكلّم معك.
dialogue.tr: ana afhamu qaleelan, wa ureedu an atakallam ma'aka.
dialogue.en: I understand a little, and I want to speak with you.
